To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a 0.7 V, 181 nW, 0.43 pJ/cycle wakeup timer for IoT applications that achieves the best energy-efficiency, long-term stability, and temperature stability over prior art.
a highly digitized architecture for a wakeup timer is presented.
a highly digitalized frequency-locked loop is used to implement a wakeup timer with the best energy efficiency and the lowest power dissipation ever reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a wakeup timer based on a digital-intensive frequency- locked loop.
the design and analysis of digital-intensive frequency- locked loops for ultra-low-power, ultra-low-voltage, high-accuracy, low-cost, low-area applications.
the development of an energy efficient and accurate wake up timer for IoT applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed timer achieves the state-of-the-art performance in terms of energy efficiency, frequency accuracy and temperature stability, thus making it a suitable candidate for low-power Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.
the proposed timer is the first wakeup timer to exploit the benefits of a digital-intensive frequency- locked loop and to operate at such low supply voltage.
the proposed timer is the best in class in terms of energy efficiency, stability and area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the timer is the most energy-efficient one among prior art, while it is also the one that has the best long-term stability and the lowest temperature sensitivity.
we have developed an ultra-low power wakeup timer with a high frequency accuracy and a high stability for IoT applications.
a highly digitized architecture is the key enabler for the design of ultra-low-power frequency generators for Internet-of- Things applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a bang-bang DCO-based frequency-locked loop is a viable alternative to a PLL-based architecture in IoT applications.

digital-intensive frequency-locking architectures are a viable alternative to traditional analog-intensive approaches for low power and low voltage applications, especially when a high frequency accuracy and a low energy consumption are required.
a highly digitalized architecture can achieve excellent frequency accuracy and low power, thus enabling a wakeup timer for low-power IoT applications.
